notice.label: Important Intellectual Property Notice
notice.heading: Bali Yoga School® Strictly Protects Its Intellectual Property
paragraphs: Bali Yoga School® strictly protects its brand, website, original photographs, videos, educational materials, course manuals, graphics, logos and other proprietary content.

Unauthorized commercial copying, reproduction, scraping, republishing, impersonation, counterfeit certification, domain-name abuse or misleading use of Bali Yoga School intellectual property may result in copyright and trademark complaints, hosting and registrar enforcement, search-engine removal requests, domain-dispute proceedings, injunctions, damages, recovery of profits and other available civil or criminal remedies.
Where justified by applicable law and the scale and willfulness of the infringement, aggregate claims may reach USD $100,000–$1,000,000 or more.

This amount is not an automatic fine. Actual liability is determined under applicable law and depends on the rights involved, registrations, number of works or marks, damages, profits, jurisdiction and other relevant circumstances.
Prior written permission is required for commercial reuse of protected Bali Yoga School materials unless the particular use is independently authorized by applicable law.
notice.footer: Legal Policy – Intellectual Property & Brand Protection. © 2019–2026 Bali Yoga School®. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 01. Purpose and Scope
paragraphs: This Intellectual Property, Copyright, Trademark, Brand, Domain, Media and Content Protection Policy establishes the ownership, permitted use and enforcement position of Bali Yoga School® concerning its intellectual property, educational materials, brand assets, online identity and proprietary content.

This Policy applies to materials appearing on or associated with: www.baliyogaschool.com and to authorized Bali Yoga School websites, social-media accounts, course materials, advertisements, training programs, photographs, videos, certificates, manuals and other media.

Except where expressly stated otherwise, no person, company, yoga school, retreat operator, teacher-training provider, travel business, publisher, agency, freelancer, competitor, domain registrant, AI company, social-media account or other third party is granted permission to commercially reproduce Bali Yoga School intellectual property simply because it is publicly accessible.

Indonesia's Copyright Law No. 28 of 2014 recognizes copyright as an exclusive right arising automatically once a work has been embodied in tangible form, subject to statutory limitations.
Accordingly, registration is not what initially creates all copyright rights; however, formal registrations and ownership records may provide important evidence and enforcement advantages.

sections.heading: 37. Indonesia – Copyright Law
paragraphs: Bali Yoga School reserves rights available under Law No. 28 of 2014 on Copyright.

The legislation recognizes copyright as an exclusive right arising automatically once a work is embodied and includes both moral and economic rights. It also establishes civil and enforcement mechanisms concerning copyright infringement.
The applicability and amount of any civil or criminal remedy depend upon the actual facts and relevant statutory provisions.

sections.heading: 38. Indonesia – Trademark Law

sections.heading: 39. Indonesia – Personal Data

sections.heading: 40. United States – Copyright Enforcement
paragraphs: Where United States copyright law applies, a copyright owner may pursue actual damages and attributable profits or, where statutory requirements are satisfied, elect statutory damages.
17 U.S.C. §504 generally provides: USD $750–$30,000 per work, with potential increase to up to USD $150,000 per work for willful infringement.
Eligibility for particular remedies depends on circumstances including ownership and registration requirements.

sections.heading: 41. United States – Trademark Counterfeiting
paragraphs: Where a case meets the statutory requirements for use of a counterfeit registered mark, U.S. law provides potential statutory damages of: $1,000–$200,000 per counterfeit mark per type of goods/services, and up to $2,000,000 per counterfeit mark per type of goods/services for willful use.
These figures are judicial remedies—not automatic private fines.

sections.heading: 42. United States – Cybersquatting
paragraphs: For qualifying violations of the U.S. Anti-Cybersquatting Consumer Protection Act, statutory damages may range from USD $1,000 to $100,000 per domain name, as determined by the court.
Not every similar domain qualifies; the statutory requirements must be proven.
